# The World Then

> An interactive atlas of world history at https://theworldthen.com — a
> time-scrubbable world map covering roughly 2000 BCE to the present, with
> ~1,250 polity records: border-geometry frames, rulers, wars, religions,
> languages, endonyms and cities. Free, no accounts, no tracking.

The map itself is a JavaScript application and not meaningfully crawlable;
the pages below carry the project's prose and provenance.

## Pages

- [The atlas](https://theworldthen.com/): the app. Deep links use a URL hash
  (#year/polity/lens), e.g. https://theworldthen.com/#1279
- [About](https://theworldthen.com/about.html): methodology, sources, licensing,
  attributions, privacy, accessibility, and the honest limits of drawing 4,000
  years of borders — every data source and asset is credited there

## Key facts

- Data: compiled ("baked") from Wikidata, Wikipedia, the historical-basemaps
  project (A. Ourednik), and Natural Earth; snapshot date shown on the About page
- Borders are approximate by design — source sheets are centuries apart in the
  ancient world, decades in the modern; the About page discloses coarseness
- Licenses: code The World Then Noncommercial ShareAlike License 1.0 (custom,
  noncommercial, share-alike with matching source; full text at
  https://theworldthen.com/LICENSE.md); curated content CC BY-NC-SA 4.0;
  border geometry GPL-3.0 (inherited); Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0; source at
  https://github.com/mikeroni/theworldthen (source/, tagged per release)
- Built with AI assistance, disclosed plainly on the About page
- Contact: see the About page
